name: Food and drink
description: Ordinary and unusual provisions, meals, and drinks

fields.description: Compact food sufficient for three days.
A fresh loaf with a crisp crust, suitable for an everyday meal.
A small wheel of firm cheese that travels and stores well.
Salted strips that keep well in a pack.
Firm salted fish smoked for travel or winter stores.
Seasonal fruit ready to eat before it spoils.
Dried, sugared, or jarred fruit prepared for a longer journey.
A practical assortment of fresh roots, greens, and seasonal produce.
Crisp seasonal vegetables preserved in a sharp brine.
A whole chicken roasted with salt and common herbs.
A generous cut of meat roasted over a fire or in an oven.
A hot, simple soup made from whatever vegetables and scraps are available.
A thick, filling stew slowly cooked from ordinary local ingredients.
A warm bowl of grain cooked with water or milk.
Several fresh eggs ready to boil, fry, bake, or trade.
A mug or stoppered jug of ordinary local ale.
A common brewed drink whose color and bitterness reflect local grain and hops.
A fermented honey drink ranging from light and dry to rich and sweet.
A fermented fruit drink, usually made from local apples or pears.
A bottle or jug whose character and quality depend on the region.
A small bottle of strong distilled drink meant to be served sparingly.
Clean drinking water stored in a sealed jug or skin.
A fragrant blend prepared for warmth, hospitality, or mild comfort.
A rare fruit whose unfamiliar shape and flavor attract curious buyers.
A distinctive dish prized locally and surprising to outsiders.
A dark savory broth made from several varieties of edible mushrooms.
